ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, an artificial satellite originally moves around Earth E in elliptical orbit 1. After changing orbit at point P, it enters orbit 2 and undergoes uniform circular motion. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Whether moving in orbit 1 or in orbit 2, the satellite has the same acceleration at point P.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an artificial satellite originally moves around Earth E in elliptical orbit 1. After changing orbit at point P, it enters orbit 2 and undergoes uniform circular motion. When the satellite moves along orbit 1 and orbit 2 respectively at point P, what is the relationship between the accelerations?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Whether moving in orbit 1 or in orbit 2, the satellite has the same acceleration at point P.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, Earth is labeled E and is located inside the orbit; the elliptical orbit is labeled 1, and the outer circular orbit is labeled 2. Both orbits pass through the same point P on the right. A dashed line passes through E from left to right and points to P, so in the two orbits, when the satellite is at point P, its distance to Earth E is the same EP. Then reason: The problem says that the satellite originally moves along elliptical orbit 1, and after changing orbit at point P, enters circular orbit 2 and undergoes uniform circular motion. What is compared is the acceleration of the satellite when it moves along the two orbits respectively at point P. If the engine thrust at the instant of orbit change is not considered, the main force on the satellite when it moves in orbit is Earth's gravitational force on it. The acceleration determined by universal gravitation is a=GM/r^2, directed toward Earth E. Since the position of point P is the same in the two cases, r=EP is the same, so the magnitude of the acceleration is the same, and the direction also points toward E.
